description: Non-ASCII letters and digits (such as é or full-width digits) are accepted in usernames and passwords, although the spec allows only ASCII
Any password logs a user in, because the typed password's hash is compared with itself instead of with the stored hash
A user's password can be changed without knowing the old password, as long as the new password is valid
Deleting or changing a user also deletes or changes every user whose name starts with the same letters (removing "bob" also removes "bobby")
Any logged-in user can read, write or delete another user's files, because the ownership check no longer runs when an owner is given
Reading from a file returns one byte too few, so the last requested byte is always missing
Reading a file returns extra padding bytes after the real data, because chunk content is no longer cut to its stored size
Decrypting a file whose plaintext ends with newline characters writes an output file with those newlines missing
Writing text that contains non-ASCII characters (such as é or emoji) silently drops those characters, so reading the file back gives different text
file_size reports one byte less than the file really holds
The last byte of every 1,024-byte block is dropped when a file is split into chunks, so files longer than a few bytes are stored corrupted
In a file with two or more chunks, the second-to-last chunk does not link to the last chunk, so multi-chunk files cannot be read back
A middle chunk that is shortened, or that links to the wrong next chunk, is accepted as long as the other condition still holds
A chunk whose size field has been changed to a value between 1,025 and 1,076 is accepted, so reading it returns header bytes as if they were file content
When a file is rewritten, its old first chunk is never deleted, so stale chunk files (holding old data) pile up on disk
A meta file that has been altered is never detected, because the expected digest is compared with itself instead of with the computed one
Every file with more than one chunk is wrongly reported as tampered, because the end name is compared with the first chunk instead of the last
Extra data added to a file's chunks is not detected and is returned to the user, because the total only has to be at least the file size
A chunk file with extra bytes appended to it is accepted, because only chunk files that are too short are rejected
A change to the first padding byte straight after a chunk's content is not detected
